question: A fair die is thrown to select one of two bags. If the die shows $1$ or $2$, Bag I is selected; otherwise Bag II is selected. Bag I contains $3$ white and $5$ black balls, while Bag II contains $6$ white and $4$ black balls. One ball is drawn from the selected bag and is found to be white. Determine the probability that Bag I had been selected.
explanation:
Given Information
Let $E_1$ and $E_2$ denote the events that Bag I and Bag II are selected respectively, and let $W$ denote the event that the drawn ball is white. Since Bag I is selected when the die shows $1$ or $2$,
$$P(E_1)=\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3},\qquad P(E_2)=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}.$$
From the compositions of the bags,
$$P(W|E_1)=\frac{3}{8},\qquad P(W|E_2)=\frac{6}{10}=\frac{3}{5}.$$

Applying Total Probability
Since $E_1$ and $E_2$ form a partition of the sample space,
$$P(W)=P(E_1)P(W|E_1)+P(E_2)P(W|E_2).$$
Thus,
$$P(W)=\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{3}{8}+\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{5}=\frac{1}{8}+\frac{2}{5}=\frac{21}{40}.$$

Applying Bayes’ Theorem
The required probability is
$$P(E_1|W)=\frac{P(E_1)P(W|E_1)}{P(W)}.$$
Therefore,
$$P(E_1|W)=\frac{\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{3}{8}}{\frac{21}{40}}=\frac{\frac{1}{8}}{\frac{21}{40}}=\frac{5}{21}.$$

Final Result
Hence, the probability that Bag I had been selected, given that the ball drawn is white, is $\frac{5}{21}$.
